basis: Inherited choroidal atrophy confined to the eye.
Thrombus occupies a coronary vessel; local thrombosis does not establish a systemic coagulation disorder.
Hirschsprung disease and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; iris coloboma and ptosis occur in 30-79%. Cardiac and urinary defects are under 30%.
Lysosomal skeletal disease; dental abnormalities and conductive hearing loss each occur in 30-79%. Nail abnormalities omitted at cap; sleep apnea separately coded.
Tumor arises in joint synovium, bursae or tendon sheaths.
Severe destructive periodontitis spans the group; palmoplantar keratoderma defines the predominant syndromic forms. Skeletal abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Defective ossification produces parietal skull openings; neurological injury and scalp defects are not established as common.
Cerebellar degeneration causes ataxia and associated neurological dysfunction; nystagmus and abnormal pursuit reflect central oculomotor disease.
Axonal degeneration affects central and peripheral nervous systems; dental pulp deposits alone do not establish dental damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; strabismus and visual dysfunction occur in 30-79%. Constipation alone and unspecified respiratory findings do not establish organ damage.
Severe Zellweger metabolic disorder; CNS dysfunction and hepatopathy are typical (>30%). Cataract and skeletal stippling lack a reliable subtype frequency.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease with neurological dysfunction; visual loss, hearing impairment and hypotonia each reported in 1/1 patients. Small sample limits certainty.
Intracranial bleeding into the subarachnoid space directly affects the CNS; aneurysm and systemic coagulation disease are not inherent to every case.
Persistent allergic inflammation of nasal airways; an immune-mediated respiratory disease.
Acute auricular perichondritis is typically a bacterial infection of the external ear's perichondrium.
Renal tubular acid-handling failure defines an acid-base disorder; rickets and hearing loss are not common across the entire group.
Retinal signaling dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity.
Inherited intestinal chloride transport failure causes persistent secretory diarrhea with defining hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
Beta-zone peripapillary atrophy affects retinal pigment epithelium and chorioretinal tissue around the optic disc.
Supplied HPO places intellectual disability, hearing loss and hepatic dysfunction at 30-79%; these frequencies reflect symptomatic disease. Blood and ocular involvement omitted at cap.
Immune-mediated giant-cell inflammation causes myocardial necrosis, fibrosis and ventricular dysfunction.
Describes a heritable vascular response to isoproterenol; cardiovascular mapping is clear, although this is a quantitative trait rather than an established damaging disease.
Defective lectin-pathway complement activation is an immunodeficiency; secondary infections do not establish a common directly damaged organ.
Disorder of cardiac impulse generation or conduction; extracardiac damage is not intrinsic across this umbrella.
Explicitly nonsyndromic early-onset cataract; the LSS gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
